_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local wild population for band5_stronghold_approach. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. New entries take an unused order in this band's reserved range 5000-5999, which no other band can collide with.
_comment_aspect_variant_0830: T3-CREATURES, from the owner's creature-expansion brief. This entry is an ASPECT VARIANT -- a rare individual whose environmental exposure changed its typing, authored as a species in data/creatures/species.json with a `variant_of` back-link. Read the brief's 'Spawn Protection Rules' section before touching count, gates or placement: its stated failure mode is exact -- 'Avoid a situation where the player walks through one clearing and sees Sparkit + Cindercub + Shadelet + Frostclaw + Nightburrow. That would destroy the rarity.' RARITY HERE IS HEADCOUNT, NOT PROBABILITY. This director does not roll a species per encounter; every cluster names its own and spawns it deterministically at load, so the brief's percentages are translated into how MANY individuals exist, WHERE, and behind WHICH gates. The chapter holds 881 wild creatures across 261 clusters, so one individual is 0.11% of the world. `respawn_seconds` overrides the table's global 45s so a rare encounter does not become a farmable resource a minute after it is beaten.
_comment_why_this_file_was_empty: WILD-ECOLOGY. Prompt 60: 'Current Band 5 empty spawn file must be reconciled' and 'not an empty faction-only corridor.' The approach to the Meadows Hall fielded Team Tether's gauntlet and nothing else alive -- so the chapter's last region, the one the whole climb has been preparing for, was also the only region where the world itself had no presence. GATEC-CURVE had authored this band's wild range as [14, 17], the strongest field in the chapter and the one that makes a late catch a genuine argument against a raised member of the five; with no clusters here that range applied to nothing at all.
_comment_habitat: Short region (z 7000-7560, ~560m of spine) and a hostile one. The read is a drained land whose animals have not left it: what is here is dug in, roosting on Team Tether's own stonework, or hunting the approach. Density is higher per metre than any other band because the region is short -- four clusters over 560m -- and that is deliberate: the last corridor should feel occupied by something other than trainers. Levels come from chapter_curve.json's band for this z, not from this file.

spawns._why: The mouth of the approach ((-80,7120) is the spine's first point past the band boundary). A burrowing ground species is the believable survivor of drained ground -- it went under it. First thing met in the region, and the least dangerous of the four.
spawns._why_rolled: T3-ENCOUNTER: ordinary ambient wildlife in rock/quarry/warrens country. Nothing authored depends on this cluster being burrowback -- no alpha/elder block, no time/weather gate, no role, no test pin, no `_why` framing it as a designed encounter. Rolled from `meadows_rock`; at world seed 0 it stands up burrowback exactly as before.

spawns._why: The approach's hunters, on the spine at (-20,7250). Galecrest is the `aggressor` role and this is the largest aggressive cluster in the chapter (3, against the usual 2) because this is the last stretch before the Hall and it should not be safer than the river crossing was. Ungated, per the head file's rule that the aggressor role is always reachable.
spawns._why_alpha: ASSESS-REDS/prompt 60's 'handful of special encounters'. The pack leader of the chapter's largest aggressor cluster, on the last stretch before the Hall -- a wild fight worth winning on its own terms in the same stretch the spec already asks to feel harder than the river crossing, not just Team Tether's own gauntlet.
spawns._comment_alpha_scale_0901: BACKLOG-VISUAL-ALPHA-SCALE. Dropped 1.4 -> 1.2 (2.94m -> 2.52m): the old value put this alpha ABOVE the Veridian Stag legendary (2.60m, D12/D19 'above every other creature in the biome'), which nobody had cross-checked since D69 raised ordinary Galecrest to 2.10m. 1.2 keeps this the tallest of the three authored Galecrest alphas (band3 1.10, band4 1.15, band5 1.20 -- an escalating ladder matching the chapter curve) while staying a clear 0.08m under Veridian and 0.37m over ordinary Tuskroot (2.15m), instead of the old 1.14x-ish separation a blind census measured and called too thin to read as a boss.

spawns._why: Roosting at the Sigil gate (playground_world.gd's SIGIL_GATE_AT, (0,7400)) on Team Tether's own masonry -- the image the region is for. Deliberately NOT night-gated: the gate is a fixed beat every player passes through once, and a nocturnal cluster there would simply be absent for most players.

spawns._why: The last 80m before the Hall ((20,7480) is the spine's final point before (0,7560)). The chapter's strongest ordinary wild creatures, standing between the player and the Warden -- the final chance to weigh a catch against the five that are about to fight the boss.

BAND5-CONTENT. Prompt 66's 'special encounter' -- one solitary, optional catch that tempts a prepared player to spend resources before the Hall. Mudsnout is deliberately the same species `stronghold_courtyard`'s Warder Solene fields (trainers.json) at level 16-17: Team Tether's own stock, escaped or turned loose off the drained ground, wilder for it. Not new lore -- it says the faction's creatures come from this same land, which the courtyard fight already implies. Sited off-spine at the `tm_heavenfall` detour (playground_world.gd's TM_AT, (140,7300)) so the same trip that risks the apex Air TM also risks this fight: two reasons to leave the road in the same 30m, not two separate errands. A LARGE radius (26m, against the ordinary clusters' 16-22m) reads as a single wary animal ranging rather than a den -- the opposite presentation from the burrowback/galecrest/duskhush/trailpup clusters, on purpose, so a prepared player can tell at a glance this is the one worth stalking rather than just another patch of aggro.

spawns._why: BAND5-DEADTRAVEL. This lane's driven run (`tools/_probe_band5_approach.gd`) walked the authored spine and measured a 123m stretch with nothing within reach of the road -- the whole eastward diagonal from (-6,7267) to (73,7361), the longest dead-travel interval in the region and the one the player crosses immediately before the gate. The density pass above added 65 creatures but sited six of its clusters OFF-spine on purpose, and this leg is where that left the road itself bare. Centred on the leg rather than beside it. Duskhush because the two nearest clusters are already duskhush (orders 5002, 5012) and the band's habitat note calls this the ground that is hunted rather than dug into -- one more of the same animal reads as a range, where a fifth species here would read as a menu.

_comment_ashtusk_removed: D71/T3-SUNSTONE, 2026-08-30. The wild Ashtusk cluster T3-CREATURES placed here (order 5100, one individual at (118,0,7340), the scorched-industrial ground by the Sigil gate) is REMOVED. The owner directed Ashtusk to be reached by evolving a Mudsnout with a Sunstone instead ('there should just be some kind of sunstone... to get the Ashtusk'), which gives Ashtusk `evolves_from: mudsnout` -- and tests/test_spawns_data.gd::test_no_evolved_form_spawns_wild already forbids any evolved-form species from spawning wild (D20: 'an evolution you can just walk up to and catch makes evolving pointless'). Keeping this cluster would have meant weakening that test, which this lane's brief explicitly forbids. The site is NOT abandoned: scripts/world/playground_world.gd now places the Sunstone pickup in this same pocket, so the ground keeps its narrative payload (this is where a fire-touched Tuskroot comes from) and the encounter becomes a genuine five-creature-slot choice rather than a catch. See ralph/reports/SUNSTONE_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md section 4 for the options considered and docs/decisions/D71 for the full record.
_comment_density_pass: BAND5-DENSITY. Owner directive, 2026-08-22: 'you're going to need a lot more than 24 creatures in a band... look at Pokemon density and Palworld density... Valheim deer and boar density it's far more.' The original five clusters/10 creatures above (plus the mudsnout special encounter) were sited against the OLD floor and are kept unchanged, positions and reasoning both -- this is an addition, not a rewrite. Orders 5005-5021 add 17 clusters/65 creatures: a cluster roughly every 35m of the spine's own ~650m length (skipping stations that already fell on an existing cluster, the outer watch or the checkpoint trainer, or landed short of the band's own z=7000 boundary), thinner (3-4, not 5) across the exposed stretch between the mouth and the Sigil gate where the original _comment_habitat's own reasoning already called the ground more dangerous than populous, plus six off-spine pockets (orders 5016-5021) so leaving the road is rewarded rather than the route reading as a conveyor belt. Total: 22 clusters, 75 creatures over ~530m of authored spine -- inside the owner's 18-28/70-110 target, toward its lower-middle rather than its ceiling, because `encounter_director.gd` instantiates and ticks every spawn in the whole 7.5km corridor with no distance-based streaming yet (a separate lane is landing that; band5 does not own either file). Species stay the four the region already established (burrowback/galecrest/duskhush/trailpup) plus mudsnout (already introduced by the special encounter, order 5004) for the direct route; the off-spine pockets add pipwing and meadowhart, both already-validated non-evolved roster species used wild elsewhere in the chapter, for the ecological variety a detour should be rewarded with.
